prior_year_events.impact_description: Primary insurance market losses in 2016 (Hurricane Matthew) impacted short-tail property loss ratios and contributed to reserve strengthening for short-tail books.
Record hailstorms in Texas in 2016 increased weather-related claims, contributing to higher loss reserves in property-related books.
Unprecedented flooding in Louisiana in 2016 increased small weather event claims and was noted as a factor in deteriorating results and reserve strengthening.

data.standardized_narrative: Syndicate 1200 reported a material strengthening of reserves in 2017, with management stating an overall deterioration of GBP 53.7m. The syndicate cites a combination of factors: a very active US catastrophe year (Hurricanes Harvey, Irma, Maria, California wildfires and a Mexico earthquake) and adverse development in short-tail classes (US Direct & Facultative, Cargo, Yachts & Hull) where prolonged rate pressure and increased facilities led to higher-than-expected losses and IBNR recalibration. The aggregate gross claims outstanding increased materially year-on-year, with most reserve increases concentrated in Property and Reinsurance acceptance exposures.
raw_causal_phrases: The very disappointing underlying performance in 2017 has been impacted by the worst year for catastrophes in the US for over a decade with Hurricanes Harvey, Irma and Maria, the wildfires in California and earthquakes in Mexico causing insured market losses of $135 billion, the costliest year on record (source: Munich Re).

Syndicate 1200 has also had to strengthen loss reserves predominantly in short tail lines of business that have seen the most rate pressure in the market over the last four years, namely US Direct & Facultative, Cargo, Yachts & Hull.
These lines have seen rate reductions of up to 50% in the last 4 years as well as unsustainable losses developing well in excess of the expected level.
This has resulted in a detailed validation plan that we started to implement in the second half of 2017.

data.data_quality_notes: Prior year development (PYD) extracted from narrative statement 'overall deterioration of GBP 53.7m' in the Risk Management note. The claims development triangle is present but includes an aggregated '2011 and prior' column and RITC activity is noted elsewhere (2015 year closed RITC), which can distort simple comparisons; the gross outstanding claims increased year-on-year by GBP 185.7m (772.3 - 586.6) but that total includes current year incurred activity; the explicit PYD sentence was used as the authoritative PYD figure. Some development table cells are blank for very recent years; computations using the triangle as a primary source were therefore limited.
